item.text: The implementation preserves the existing `streamer` and `bot` token namespaces and gives the second Keeper its own token, lease and encryption context. Keeper callbacks now rotate role-scoped control cookies, so authorizing the second account does not replace the home account’s control session. I’m testing account isolation, refresh, CSRF and persisted session behavior in both adapters.

p=Path('src/runtime.js');s=p.read_text().replace(\"if (env.KEEPER_CHANNEL_IDS && "'!keeperIds.every(id => ['"'1591805230', '1591806023'].includes(id)))\", \"if (env.KEEPER_CHANNEL_IDS && ("'!keeperIds.every(id => ['"'1591805230', '1591806023'].includes(id)) || env.TWITCH_STREAMER_ID "'!== '"'1591805230' || env.TWITCH_BOT_ID "'!== '"'1591804828'))\");p.write_text(s)
p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text();idx=s.index('## Deployed foundation handoff');s=s[:idx]+'''## Local next increment: two-Keeper OAuth and private control sessions

Not deployed by Codex. The owner authorizes the parent to redeploy this feature after review/gates; the currently verified runtime remains "'`74f490123acc982eaa0426ff9b9ffb33369f2fd9`. Readiness stays foundation/not-ready-for-raids. Worker/bootstrap actions are **not implemented in this increment**; no stub reports success.

For the two-account configuration set `KEEPER_CHANNEL_IDS=1591805230,1591806023`, primary streamer `1591805230` (raidrelichq), bot `1591804828` (raidrelicbot), public client `6ggythtvgo572dxu8jo4xoaqtn37ix`. These are the only allowed runtime IDs when the explicit Keeper list is supplied; arbitrary OAuth paths fail closed. The default single configured account remains compatible. `/oauth/keeper/1591805230/start` and `/oauth/keeper/1591806023/start` use the same exact allowlisted `/auth/callback` redirect. Legacy `/oauth/streamer/start` remains home, `/oauth/bot/start` remains bot. Keepers request only `channel:bot channel:manage:raids`; bot retains its three existing scopes. No live consent or Twitch grant validation was performed here.

Home tokens/leases/AES-GCM AAD retain the `streamer` namespace; bot is unchanged; second Keeper uses `keeper:1591806023`. `accessTokenForKeeper(id)` strictly selects configured accounts and validates identity/client/scopes on access and refresh; legacy `accessToken('"'streamer')"'` aliases home. No home/second token substitution is accepted. OAuth state remains one-use/expiring/browser-bound; sequential flows preserve previously issued role-scoped control cookies.

Successful Keeper consent creates a fresh 32-byte random **control session**, one current session per Keeper (maximum two configured accounts), stored hash-only with role, Keeper ID, expiry and hashed CSRF verifier. A new consent rotates that Keeper'"'s session and invalidates its old cookie; it leaves the other Keeper's control session intact. Sessions expire after one hour with no sliding extension. Production cookies are Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/ with "'`__Host-` names per Keeper. Bot consent creates no Keeper session. OAuth denial/error/replay creates none. Control logout deletes only the application control session, **not Twitch authorization or encrypted tokens**.

`GET /control/<keeperId>` is a scoped private shell; unauthenticated requests return 401 with the exact Keeper connection link. `GET /control/<keeperId>/status` returns only its Keeper ID/expiry, session-bound CSRF and currently allowed action `logout`, never OAuth tokens. No-store/no-referrer apply. `POST /control/<keeperId>` accepts only JSON `{ "action": "logout", "csrf": "<own-session-CSRF>" }`, exact `Content-Type: application/json`, at most 1024 bytes, and exact canonical Origin (OAuth redirect origin). Missing/wrong Origin, duplicate/missing/wrong-role cookies, expired/replaced session, extra fields, invalid CSRF or unsupported actions fail closed. Internal `oauth.control.authorizePost` provides the same scoped authorization contract for the next reviewed increment; it does not dispatch worker or bootstrap effects. Service callers must still transactionally bind any future privileged mutation to the authorized session. No public actor IDs or returnTo redirects are trusted.

Memory and fake-Firestore tests cover two consents, same-browser roles, denial/account/scope errors, encrypted context isolation, refresh/legacy compatibility, rotation/expiry, CSRF/origin/body/action/cookie failures, hash-only records and logout isolation.
